# Paired-device access

What a device's own token may reach once the pairing flow has minted it. A phone or
desktop can be lost or rooted, so the token is **denied by default**: it may send the
WebSocket commands, reach the REST routes and hear the event types below, and nothing
else. Both auth doors read these tables (`WebSocketHandler._dispatch`,
`rest.require_token`), so a route added tomorrow is refused until it is listed in
`aura-core/aura/paired_access.py` on purpose. Anything off a table answers the same
fixed `forbidden` ("this token may not do this").

This is a door, not a sandbox: handlers narrow some allowed commands further, and a
caller holding the house token (the Hermes plugins, the adapter's relays) is not a
paired token and is not limited here. The runbook
([connectors](../runbooks/connectors.md)) says what the door does not cover.

13 WebSocket commands, 16 REST routes, 16 event types.

## WebSocket commands

| Command | Client that needs it |
| --- | --- |
| `ping` | phone DeviceLink/JarvisChannel keepalive; desktop channel.py heartbeat |
| `jarvis/device/register` | phone JarvisChannel and desktop channel.py: announce the device and its abilities |
| `subscribe_events` | phone AssistPipelineClient and TaskFrames: the turn's and the tasks' event feed |
| `conversation/process` | phone DeviceLink and JarvisConversation: a typed turn |
| `assist_pipeline/run` | phone AssistPipelineClient and CompanionVoiceClient: a voice turn |
| `assist_pipeline/pipeline/list` | phone AssistPipelineClient: which pipelines exist |
| `jarvis/approve` | phone ApprovalBridge: answer a consent from the phone's own screen |
| `jarvis/notes/list` | phone JarvisConversation: the notes shown beside a turn |
| `jarvis/memory/list` | phone JarvisConversation: the memory shown beside a turn |
| `jarvis/notifications/list` | phone MomentWatch: the notification feed |
| `jarvis/tasks/list` | phone TaskFrames: the task list |
| `jarvis/surface/list` | phone SurfaceWatch: what the house put on the surface |
| `jarvis/surface/remove` | phone SurfaceWatch: dismiss a surface card |

| `GET /api/notes` | desktop actions/notes.py: find_note |
| `POST /api/notes` | desktop actions/notes.py: save_note |
| `GET /api/notes/{note_id}` | desktop actions/notes.py: find_note by id |
| `GET /api/voice/speaker` | phone VoiceIdentityClient and desktop enrol_client.py: who is enrolled |
| `POST /api/voice/speaker/enrol` | phone VoiceIdentityClient and desktop enrol_client.py: enrol a voice |
| `POST /api/voice/speaker/enrolling` | phone VoiceIdentityClient: enrolment progress |
| `POST /api/voice/speaker/verify` | phone VoiceIdentityClient: check a voice sample |
| `POST /api/voice/speaker/people` | phone VoiceIdentityClient: the People screen's write |
| `DELETE /api/voice/speaker` | phone VoiceIdentityClient and desktop enrol_client.py: forget a voice |
| `GET /api/models/{name}` | phone ModelStore: download an on-device model |
| `GET /api/maps/regions` | phone car/holo MapPackSync: which map packs exist |
| `GET /api/maps/packs/{region}` | phone car/holo MapPackSync: download a map pack |
| `POST /api/maps/route` | phone car/holo HouseMaps: a route |
| `POST /api/maps/match` | phone car/holo HouseMaps: snap a fix to the road |
| `GET /api/maps/buildings` | phone car/holo HouseMaps: buildings near the car |
| `GET /api/maps/live` | phone car/holo HouseMaps: live overlays near the car |

## Event types

`subscribe_events` on a paired socket names exactly one of these: no missing type, no
`*`, so the feed is not the whole bus.

| Event | Client that needs it |
| --- | --- |
| `jarvis_tool_started` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `jarvis_tool_finished` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `jarvis_task_added` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `jarvis_task_updated` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `state_changed` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `jarvis_mqtt_event` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `vision_look_started` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `vision_look_finished` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `vision_look_denied` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `memory_changed` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `jarvis_notification` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `jarvis_approval_required` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `jarvis_approval_resolved` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `jarvis_speaker_verdict` | phone AssistPipelineClient: ActivityRows.EVENTS, the strip's whole vocabulary |
| `jarvis_task_removed` | phone JarvisChannel.watchTasks: TaskBoard.EVENTS |
| `jarvis_surface_changed` | phone JarvisChannel.watchSurface: SurfaceWatch.EVENT |

## The approver switch

`jarvis/approve` is on the list because the phone is the owner's approval surface, so a
paired token may answer any held request and a stolen one can approve until it is
revoked. The owner's `approver` switch on the token (owner-only, on for a new pairing)
is the narrower remedy for a device that should never approve: with it off the token is
refused `jarvis/approve` and is not sent these two events, read live on an open socket.

`jarvis_approval_required`, `jarvis_approval_resolved`
